item.title: 2027: Immigration vows to block foreign mercenaries, illicit arms
item.description: The Nigeria Immigration Service NIS has pledged to tighten surveillance at the nation’s borders ahead of the 2027 general election, as sister security agencies named foreign mercenaries and illicit arms among the threats it must help keep out of the electoral process. Comptroller General of the Immigration Service, Kemi Nana Nandap, made the pledge on Friday in Abuja at a sensitisation workshop on election security for senior personnel, themed “The strategic role of the NIS in Election Monitoring and intimidation”. “As we prepare for the 2027 general elections, let us be guided by the common purpose to protect our national security, uphold the rule of law, and contribute to an electoral environment in which every Nigerian can exercise their democratic rights peacefully and without intimidation.” Represented by the Deputy Comptroller General DCG in charge of Visa and Residency, Dr Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, the immigration boss said, “As the agency charged with the mandate of border security and migration management, we occupy a strategic position in the nation’s security architecture. We must therefore remain alert to the influx of foreigners, particularly irregular migration, trafficking in persons, smuggling of migrants, and other transnational criminal activities capable of undermining national security.” The Comptroller General stressed that the service cannot do this alone. “No single agency can address the complex security challenges confronting our nation in isolation,” the address said, appreciating “the continued partnership” of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC and other security agencies. Warning the personnel against partisanship, the immigration boss said, “Let us therefore reiterate that the Nigeria Immigration Service remains a non-partisan institution. Under no circumstances should our personnel use official resources to promote partisan interests. “You must ensure that our commands are adequately prepared before, during, and after elections through strengthening surveillance, intelligence gathering, effective deployment, and close coordination with relevant security agencies,” she said. In inter-agency work, the CG said the service’s participation in the Interagency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES must be proactive, purposeful, and result-orientated. “I expect every senior officer to lead by example and take full responsibility for maintaining professional standards within their respective formats,” she stated. In his remarks, Director General, Department of State Services DSS, Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi told the gathering that electoral periods attract attempts to exploit the nation’s frontiers for the movement of “illicit arms, mercenaries” and others bent on undermining the democratic process. item.title: Iran seeks stronger economic, political ties with Nigeria
item.description: Iranian President Dr Masoud Pezeshkian has underscored the need to deepen Nigeria-Iran economic, political and cultural ties to harness untapped potential and enhance bilateral cooperation between both countries. Pezeshkian ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌‌⁠⁠‌‍‌‌​said this while receiving the Letters of Credence presented to him by Nigeria’s Ambassador to Iran, Amb. Hamza Sallau, during an official diplomatic engagement in Tehran. This is contained in a statement issued on Friday in Abuja by Mr Oluwafemi Adeniyi, spokesperson for Nigeria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. He reiterated Iran’s commitment to identifying and pursuing new opportunities aimed at strengthening diplomatic relations and delivering mutually beneficial outcomes for both countries. Earlier, Sallau conveyed the warm greetings of President Bola Tinubu to President Pezeshkian and the people of Iran, reaffirming Nigeria’s commitment to deepening bilateral relations. According to him, trade, agriculture and healthcare are priority areas for enhanced collaboration between the two countries to promote economic growth and strengthen cooperation. The envoy commended both countries’ shared commitment to multilateralism and international cooperation, saying the Nigeria-Iran Joint Commission should be prioritised as a mechanism to advance bilateral cooperation. He added that the commission should identify new practical areas for mutually beneficial partnerships between the two countries, while strengthening existing diplomatic and economic ties. Both parties restated their commitment to expanding political engagement, strengthening institutional cooperation and promoting people-to-people relations between Nigeria and Iran. The presentation of the Letters of Credence by Sallau formally marked his accreditation as Nigeria’s Ambassador Plenipotentiary and Extraordinary to the Islamic Republic of Iran. It also reflects Nigeria’s continued commitment to pursuing mutually beneficial relations with Iran in furtherance of its foreign policy objectives. item.title: Pochettino poised to agree 2.5-year deal at Man Utd
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino is set to agree a two-and-a-half-year deal to take charge of beleaguered Manchester United following the sacking of Michael Carrick, reports said Friday. The Athletic said an agreement had been reached with the USA head coach over a contract that would keep the 54-year-old at Old Trafford until 2029. Pochettino is set to take charge of his team’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final ties against Haiti on Saturday and next Tuesday before heading to Manchester. An announcement on his future could come as early as Friday, with the Argentinian set to hold a press conference previewing the first leg against Haiti at 1415 GMT. US Soccer is understood to have accepted that Pochettino is stepping down. The federation is set to receive $10 million in compensation for him plus a further $2 million for the departure of his coaching staff. Carrick was dismissed on Thursday following intense speculation over his future after a disastrous start to the season. The 20-time English champions are in the relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 matches in the Premier League so far. Carrick, who won multiple trophies as a midfielder in the club’s golden era under Alex Ferguson, is the seventh permanent manager to be dismissed by the club since the Scot retired in 2013. Pochettino guided World Cup co-hosts the USA to the last 16 of the tournament earlier this year before signing a contract extension taking him through to the 2030 World Cup. He has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. One early issue for Pochettino to wrestle with could be the future of United captain Bruno Fernandes, who has been the club’s outstanding performer for many seasons. The Portuguese attacking midfielder is understood to have rejected a second contract offer. The Red Devils have an option to extend his deal to the end of the 2027/2028 season, meaning he would not be free to talk to other clubs in January. United’s next game is against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. The post Pochettino poised to agree 2.5-year deal at Man Utd appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerian Microbiologist Bridget Ugochi Anyanwueze develops improved laboratory method to advance antimicrobial drug discovery and research
item.description: Her research introduces a time-dependent approach to measuring bacterial inhibition, offering additional information that could support the laboratory evaluation of potential antimicrobial compounds. As antimicrobial resistance continues to threaten global health, researchers are investigating new compounds capable of inhibiting bacterial growth and improving the laboratory methods used to evaluate their activity. Among these efforts is the research of microbiologist Bridget Ugochi Anyanwueze, whose work examines how antibiotic inhibition zones develop over time and how these measurements could contribute to future antimicrobial investigations. Her sole-authored research paper, “An Improved in vitro Method for Quantifying the Kinetics of Bacterial Inhibition-Zone Development,” was published on June 27, 2026, in the IPS Journal of Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology, with link to article https://doi.org/10.54117/ijamb.v6i2.170 . The study was conducted within her broader research interests in microbiology and antimicrobial activity, with her affiliation listed as the Department of Biology at Southeast Missouri State University, Cape Girardeau, United States. The research addresses a limitation of the traditional Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion assay, a laboratory method used to assess bacterial susceptibility to antibiotics. Traditionally, the method measures the diameter of the clear zone surrounding an antibiotic disc after a specified incubation period. Although this measurement provides important information about bacterial susceptibility, it does not describe how the inhibition zone develops during the preceding hours. Anyanwueze investigated whether repeated measurements could provide additional information about the progression of bacterial inhibition. Using Staphylococcus epidermidis as the test organism, she examined inhibition-zone development following exposure to ampicillin, erythromycin, and neomycin. Measurements were collected at 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, and 25 hours of incubation, allowing changes in inhibition-zone diameter and expansion rate to be examined over time. The findings revealed that the antibiotics exhibited different patterns of inhibition-zone development. Ampicillin produced the greatest absolute increase in inhibition-zone diameter, expanding by 10.23 millimetres, while erythromycin demonstrated the highest percentage expansion at 137.9%. The study also found that inhibition zones generally expanded more rapidly during earlier observations before slowing at later incubation intervals. These differences demonstrate that final inhibition-zone diameters do not capture every aspect of how inhibition zones develop. By incorporating repeated measurements, the improved approach provides additional quantitative information about the progression of measurable bacterial growth inhibition. item.title: We won’t jump to conclusions over NDC attack – Lagos APC
item.description: The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) says it will not jump to conclusions or make needless assumptions over the disruption of a political gathering organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Ikeja. The party’s spokesman, Mr Seye Oladejo, said this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) while responding to questions on the alleged attack on NDC members and the party’s denial of involvement in the incident. Oladejo said APC was a party governed by the principles of law and order and would not engage in speculative conclusions over the circumstances surrounding the incident. “We’re a party governed by law and order. However, we won’t jump the gun and embark on needless assumptions,” he said. He, however, urged Nigerians not to overlook what he described as recent threats by opposition political parties to unleash mayhem in the state. “The threats to unleash mayhem by the opposition parties recently should not be lost on the public. “Our democracy cannot thrive on anarchy and disorderly conduct,” he said. Oladejo said the APC remained committed to democratic principles, peaceful political engagement and respect for the rule of law. He stressed that political competition should not be allowed to degenerate into violence, intimidation or activities capable of undermining democratic institutions. The spokesman urged political parties and their supporters to exercise restraint and conduct their activities within the ambit of the law, particularly as political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gathered momentum. He also reiterated the need for security agencies to remain vigilant and discharge their constitutional responsibilities to prevent threats to public peace. Oladejo said political differences should be resolved through lawful democratic processes rather than actions capable of creating tension and disorder. He maintained that the APC would continue to pursue its political activities through persuasion, issue-based campaigns, grassroots mobilisation and the ballot box. NAN reports that Lagos APC, in a statement on Thursday by Oladejo, denied allegations that it sponsored the disruption of an NDC political gathering in Ikeja. The party described the allegation as reckless, baseless and irresponsible, insisting that it neither sponsored, encouraged nor participated in any action capable of undermining the constitutional rights of opposition parties. It said the alleged incident occurred on the same day APC held the official flag-off of its 2027 general election campaign in Epe, several kilometres away from Ikeja. According to the statement, the party’s leaders, elected representatives, executives, campaign officials and other stakeholders were mobilised for the Epe event. APC also accused opposition political elements of making threats to unleash violence and render the political atmosphere ungovernable. item.title: 2027: We received phone call from Buhari’s grave to vote Atiku — Dalung
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde A former Minister of Sports and Youth Development, Solomon Dalung, has claimed that supporters of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) received a phone call from the grave of former President Muhammadu Buhari, urging them to vote for the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in the 2027 election. Dalung, an ADC chieftain, made the remark on Thursday while speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he also linked the alleged message to a recent visit by Buhari’s widow, Aisha, to Atiku in Abuja. “Last month you saw when the wife of the late president visited Atiku in Abuja. The message she took for any politician to know is that the 12 million votes have been successfully transferred. We have had a phone call from the grave of Buhari that we should vote Atiku,” he said. Dalung argued that Atiku had inherited the political structures of both Buhari and former President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, giving him a nationwide political network. He also dismissed the possibility of President Bola Tinubu defeating Atiku in 2027, saying the ADC candidate would remain difficult to overcome even if the ruling party prevented the opposition from campaigning. “I am confident that as events are unfolding, Tinubu, even if he would take over the ADC secretariat and stop ADC from campaigning, he cannot defeat Atiku Abubakar in 2027,” he said. He alleged that President Tinubu is scared of 2027 election saying, “I have never seen a weak president in an election like Bola Ahmed Tinubu. If you drag anybody on the street and put him on a ballot at a contest with Tinubu, he will defeat him,” he said. item.title: Tinubu’s govt using EFCC to blackmail governors into APC — Makinde alleges
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has accused the President Bola Tinubu-led administration of using the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to intimidate governors and pressure them into joining the ruling All Progressives Congress. Makinde, who spoke during an interview on Arise News on Friday, alleged that opposition governors who refuse to defect to the APC risk being subjected to investigations and blackmail, warning that the development could undermine Nigeria’s multiparty democracy. “What we’ve seen is, well, okay, I have the governors, they come to APC. If you don’t, you will be blackmailed,” Makinde said. To illustrate his claim, he described a situation in which a contractor working for an opposition-controlled state could face scrutiny over government contracts and financial transactions. “The EFCC will come down from that place. ‘Look, how much did they award this to you? Go and bring your account. Who have you been paying?’ That is the situation that we are facing today,” he said. Makinde also alleged that the Federal Government tried to blackmail him over the Bodija explosion intervention funds, saying his administration had already compensated affected property owners before receiving federal assistance. He said the state engaged the Nigerian Society of Engineers and valuers to assess the damage and determine payments to victims. “We’ve spent the money. We got Nigerian Society of Engineers. We got valuers. You know, they went out there, had valuation of the properties, and then we gave money back to those people, and we did it before even getting anything from the federal,” he said. He added that he released the state’s account of the transaction when the issue was raised and directed the Commissioner for Finance to channel the funds into projects. Makinde did not provide evidence during the interview that the president or the APC had directed the EFCC to investigate opposition governors or their contractors. item.title: 2027 Elections: My Loyalty Is Solely To The Constitution, Says INEC Chairman Amupitan
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, has declared that his loyalty is solely to the Nigerian Constitution and the Electoral Act, insisting that his leadership of the electoral body will remain impartial. Amupitan stated this n on Thursday while responding to questions about his neutrality at Chatham House, London, during a high-level dialogue organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI). The dialogue was held under the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” His comments followed the controversy that surrounded an X (formerly Twitter) account allegedly linked to him, which allegedly made a partisan post expressing support for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) during the 2023 general elections. INEC had, however, denied that Amupitan operated the account, describing the allegations as digital impersonation. Responding to the issue at Chatham House on Thursday, the INEC chairman denied operating an X account, saying an independent forensic review had been obtained and the matter formally referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Inspector-General of Police for investigation. Amupitan (right) spoke at Chatham House on Thursday, November 12, 2026. (Photo: X/@inecnigeria) Dismissing concerns about his impartiality, Amupitan said his allegiance was to the country’s legal framework rather than any political interest. “My loyalty is solely to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the Electoral Act,” he declared. “Every constitutional institution—including the Presidency, the National Assembly, and state governors—owes its primary loyalty to the Constitution and the rule of law.” The INEC chairman also dismissed suggestions that his previous legal representation in political disputes could compromise his neutrality, explaining that he acted strictly within his professional responsibilities as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria before his appointment. Amupitan urged Nigerians to trust his leadership to conduct free, fair, and credible elections in 2027, citing improvements recorded in recent off-cycle elections and technical safeguards introduced by the commission. He acknowledged that the controversies surrounding the 2023 presidential election had significantly damaged public confidence in INEC. “First and foremost, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. He added that the commission had learnt lessons from subsequent elections, including those in Anambra and Osun states, where results were declared the day after voting. Meanwhile, Amupitan identified insecurity, logistics and result management as the commission’s major priorities ahead of the 2027 elections. item.title: Just in: Court orders INEC to publish Adebutu’s name as Ogun PDP gov candidate
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to, within 24 hours, publish Oladipupo Adebutu’s name as Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)’s candidate for the 2027 Ogun governorship election. Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgment, held that INEC had no powers to unilaterally remove the name of a validly nominated candidate by a political party. Justice Lifu held that the commission’s action was unconstitutional, unlawful and was of no effect. Justice Lifu said that it is only the Federal High Court or the state’s high court that has the power to declare a candidate invalid and not the commission. He held that INEC breached Adebutu’s right to fair hearing. The judge, who dismissed the preliminary objection filed by INEC, declared that the suit was competent. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the PDP and Adebutu had, on Oct. 22, filed the suit following the removal of Adebutu’s name from the list of contestants of the governorship seat in Ogun. The plaintiffs sued INEC as the sole defendant in the suit filed by their lawyer, Ahmed Raji, SAN. The plaintiffs, who sought six questions for determination, prayed the court for 11 reliefs. They sought an order setting aside the commission’s decision to omit, remove or refuse to publish Adebutu’s name in the final list of candidates published on Oct. 10 for denial of a fair hearing and violation of the provisions of Section 29 and Section 32 of the Electoral Act, 2026. They also sought an order directing or compelling “the defendant to, within twenty-four (24) hours of the order/orders of this honourable court, include and/or publish the name of the 2nd plaintiff as the 1st plaintiff’s governorship candidate for Ogun State in the forthcoming 2027 General Election,” among other reliefs. item.title: 2027: INEC rules out inaccurate IReV uploads
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has built strict validation safeguards into its system to prevent inaccurate results or figures reflecting over-voting from being uploaded to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). Prof. Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, gave the assurance at the Chatham House, London, during a high-level dialogue convened in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) under the theme “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot”. Thus is contained in a statement issued by the Chief Press Secretary to the INEC chairman, Mr Adedayo Oketola, in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja.’ Amupitan therefore urged Nigerians to trust his leadership to deliver free, fair and credible general elections in 2027. He highlighted measurable operational improvements recorded in recent off-cycle polls and new technical safeguards designed to prevent a repeat of the 2023 election controversies. On the trust deficit left by the 2023 presidential election, Amupitan acknowledged that the controversies surrounding that exercise severely dented public confidence in the electoral body. “First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC, damage so large that the commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. Amupitan, who assumed office in October 2025, noted that INEC had treated every subsequent election as a practical laboratory to identify operational weaknesses and strengthen accreditation, voting and result management. Responding to a question on why Nigerians should trust his leadership ahead of 2027, he cited the successful conduct of recent off-cycle elections, including the Ekiti, Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, and 16 legislative bye-elections. “Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections, and observers agree that the recent election in Osun marked a clear improvement. “Every election is a lesson. The 2023 general election was a major lesson for Nigeria, and the Anambra election was another,” he said. He noted that Anambra and Osun previously had histories of prolonged, inconclusive governorship contests, recalling that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude. He, however, said targeted administrative reforms under his watch enabled results in both states to be declared the day after voting. item.title: Oriire: Tinubu never spoke to me over abducted pupils, teachers — Makinde
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has said President Bola Tinubu failed to contact him during the 56 days pupils and teachers abducted in the state remained in captivity, despite his efforts to reach the president. Makinde said he expected Tinubu to call or show concern over the incident, which involved the abduction of schoolchildren and their teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of the state. The governor made this known during an interview with Arise Television on Friday, while discussing his relationship with Tinubu, whom he supported in the 2023 presidential election. “I tried to see the President when our students and our children and their teachers were kidnapped, because I thought if any part of Nigeria is going through such a challenge, the president should be interested. Actually, I expected the president to call me,” he said. Asked whether Tinubu eventually contacted him, Makinde replied, “He did not. No. Till tomorrow.” The governor added that he also tried reaching the president through the State Chief of Protocol but received no response to his call. Makinde maintained that he had never spoken directly with Tinubu, stressing that he was focused on governing Oyo State. “I’m saying it again that till tomorrow I’ve not spoken directly with the President about anything. I’m just minding my own business, running Oyo State. And I’m not complaining,” he said. The governor’s remarks come months after the abducted pupils and teachers regained their freedom following 56 days in captivity. The victims were seized on May 15, 2026, when gunmen attacked schools in the area. The Nigerian Army announced their rescue on July 10 after a security operation involving multiple agencies. item.title: Makinde scores Tinubu administration 34 per cent
item.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has scored President Bola Tinubu’s administration 34 per cent, saying the government has failed to secure the support of a majority of Nigerians. Makinde gave the assessment during an interview with Arise Television, where he was asked to evaluate the administration’s performance in infrastructure, diplomacy and economic growth. He likened the score to the percentage of Nigerians who supported Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, arguing that the President needed to win over those who voted against him to build a national consensus. “It’s just about the same percentage as the people that supported him in 2023, 34 per cent. You need the 66 per cent of Nigerians that were against him in 2023 to be on board. This is a national project,” he said. The governor also criticised what he described as pressure on elected officials to join the ruling All Progressives Congress, alleging that some governors were compelled to defect. “Look at what we’ve seen. You have the governors come to APC. If you don’t, you’ll be blackmailed,” he said. Makinde, who is seeking the presidency in 2027 under the Action Peoples Party (APM), also addressed whether he would accept defeat if the election was free, fair and credible. Responding to a question on whether he would concede defeat and retire to farming, the governor said he would accept the outcome if the electoral process met the required standards. “There are a few things that must happen. If the process is free, fair, and credible, yes, I will,” he said. However, when asked whether he would remain in the APM after the election, Makinde said his political future would depend on how Nigerians received his political agenda. “I may evaluate my political future depending on how Nigerians, you know, see this agenda,” he added. item.title: 5 smartphones with the best zoom cameras in 2026
item.description: Smartphone cameras have become increasingly sophisticated in 2026, with manufacturers competing to deliver sharper photographs, improved low-light performance and, particularly, better zoom capabilities. One of the biggest developments has been the introduction of more advanced periscope telephoto cameras, larger image sensors and optical zoom systems capable of capturing distant subjects without relying entirely on digital enlargement. These improvements have made it possible to photograph wildlife, sporting events, concerts, buildings and other distant subjects with a level of detail that was previously difficult to achieve with a smartphone. While several manufacturers advertise zoom capabilities of up to 100x or 120x, the actual quality of photographs at those magnifications varies considerably. Optical zoom, sensor size, optical image stabilisation and image processing are therefore more important considerations than the maximum zoom figure alone. Here are five smartphones with some of the best zoom camera systems available in 2026, based on their camera hardware and independent reviews. 1. Oppo Find X9 Ultra The Oppo Find X9 Ultra stands out as one of the most capable zoom smartphones of 2026, particularly because it features two dedicated telephoto cameras rather than relying on a single zoom lens. The smartphone comes with a 200-megapixel primary telephoto camera offering 3x optical zoom and a separate 50-megapixel periscope telephoto camera capable of 10x optical zoom. The combination gives users greater flexibility when photographing subjects at different distances, from portraits and street photography to distant buildings, wildlife and performers at concerts. Its 10x optical zoom is particularly important because it allows the camera to magnify distant subjects using its dedicated optical hardware rather than simply enlarging pixels digitally. According to Digital Trends, the phone can extend its zoom capabilities to 120x digitally. Its 200-megapixel telephoto camera also provides additional room for cropping images while retaining useful detail. The publication highlights the phone’s impressive telephoto sharpness, autofocus performance and ability to capture distant subjects. For people who regularly photograph sporting events, wildlife or concerts, the Find X9 Ultra is a particularly compelling option. 2. Huawei Pura 80 Ultra The Huawei Pura 80 Ultra is another smartphone that deserves recognition for its unusual approach to long-range photography. Its biggest attraction is a switchable dual-telephoto camera system that offers 3.7x and 9.4x optical zoom. Unlike conventional smartphones that use separate telephoto sensors for different magnification levels, Huawei developed a system in which two telephoto lenses share a large 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch sensor. item.title: Disgruntled US tenant kills building manager, injures four, shoots self
item.description: A disgruntled tenant shot dead his building manager and wounded four other people in an upscale neighborhood of Washington on Thursday before killing himself, police said amid a massive law enforcement response that shut down part of the city. The shooting, which occurred about a mile north of the White House, sparked a massive police response in the nation’s capital with dozens of law enforcement vehicles racing to the scene and police helicopters hovering overhead. Dramatic dispatch audio captured the initial callout for a shooting inside the gym just before 8 am (0100 GMT). Within minutes a breathless police officer could be heard telling the dispatcher “we have an active shooter” and requesting the SWAT team. Jeffery Carroll, Washington’s interim police chief, told reporters that the gunman, identified as Matt Lambert, 55, had been involved in an ongoing dispute over maintenance with the condominium association for the building where he owned an apartment. Lambert, an emergency medicine physician, fatally shot the building manager, James Stuart, 46, in a packed gym attached to the complex, located in the Logan Circle neighborhood. Lambert then barricaded himself in his seventh-floor unit, Carroll said. He then opened fire from his balcony on people below, wounding four. One of the wounded was in critical condition while the others did not have life-threatening injuries. The Washington Post reported that construction workers from a nearby jobsite were among the injured, citing a company executive. Lambert fired at least twice at police through his apartment door and set the unit on fire before shooting himself, Carroll said. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Photos and video quickly emerged on social media of police in tactical gear surrounding the building with rifles drawn as well as fire emerging from an exterior wall. Carroll said Lambert had taken legal action against the homeowners association of the condominium complex where he lived over what he considered to be a lack of maintenance of the building. An X feed reportedly linked to Lambert titled @OfMiceandMold is a litany of complaints about mold and water damage. The final post, described as a “manifesto,” is an engineering report detailing problems with his apartment. Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser denounced what she described as a “senseless act of gun violence.” The shooting occurred during the busy morning rush hour, snarling traffic as police closed off streets around the area and evacuated residents. The Washington Sun quoted a member of the VIDA Fitness gym as saying that he was on a treadmill at the workout facility when the shooting began. Michael Carney said he heard a “pop” and then saw someone on the gym floor who had been shot in the head. “Everyone was kind of just hiding behind planters and stuff,” Carney told The Sun. item.title: Obi leads NDC supporters in singing old national anthem in Lagos
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), on Thursday joined party supporters in singing Nigeria’s former national anthem, ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’, at a town hall meeting in Lagos. Obi, alongside Funso Doherty, the party’s governorship candidate in Lagos State, and other attendees, declined to stand for the recital of the current national anthem when prompted by the event anchor. The anchor subsequently switched to the old anthem, which Obi and the supporters sang together. During the recital, Obi faced the crowd with two fingers raised on both hands, forming a gesture associated with the NDC logo. A video of the incident, which has since circulated on social media, showed the party supporters enthusiastically singing the former national anthem. The development comes amid controversy surrounding the reintroduction of the old anthem by President Bola Tinubu. On May 29, 2024, Tinubu signed the National Anthem Bill into law, restoring ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’ as the country’s official anthem, replacing ‘Arise, O Compatriots’. The old anthem was first adopted at Nigeria’s independence on October 1, 1960, and remained in use until 1978, when it was replaced. Meanwhile, the town hall meeting was earlier disrupted when suspected thugs reportedly invaded the venue with cutlasses, cudgels and stones, forcing attendees to flee for safety. Obi previously secured victory in Lagos State during the 2023 presidential election as the Labour Party candidate, polling 582,354 votes against Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who received 572,606 votes. item.title: US lawmakers summon Nvidia ex-CEO after affair with suspected spy
item.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters. “Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote Thursday on X. Scott said he was requesting Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs. It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena. Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. While Nvidia’s board searches for a permanent successor to Huang, who spent 33 years at the helm of the firm he co-founded, chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. Nvidia hit gold when the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022 sparked a global rush to develop AI, with its processors — once designed for video game graphics — becoming a crucial ingredient to train and run the technology. – Informal Trump adviser – Nvidia did not give a reason for the departure of Huang, who also gave up his board seat. Huang is Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to the company. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI, and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry”. But he said the board had done what it needed: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him.” The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair, and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. item.title: Abductors of FUNAAB graduate, three others demand N500m ransom
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The abductors of a recent graduate of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), Adedoja Hannah, and three other individuals have reportedly demanded a ransom of N500 million for their release. The victims were allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday night when suspected gunmen invaded a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta, Ogun State, where they were working. The development was disclosed by the Students’ Union Government (SUG) of FUNAAB in a statement posted on its official Facebook platform on Thursday, expressing concern over the safety of the victims and appealing to members of the university community and the general public to remain calm. According to the union, Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, was among the four people abducted during the incident. Providing an account of the circumstances surrounding her disappearance, the union stated that Hannah was last seen on Monday, while her telephone has remained unreachable since the reported abduction. The statement partly reads, “The Students’ Union Government wishes to update the FUNAAB community and the general public on the abduction of Adedoja Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), alongside three other individuals at a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta. “According to information received, the incident occurred on Tuesday night when suspected kidnappers reportedly invaded the farm where the victims were working. Hannah was last seen on Monday, and her phone has remained unreachable since the incident. “Further information indicates that the abductors have demanded a ransom of ₦500 million for the release of all four victims. This development has understandably heightened concerns over their safety and the circumstances surrounding the incident. “The incident was reported to the appropriate security authorities, and the police have been working on the matter since Tuesday. Security efforts are ongoing, with attention directed towards locating the victims and securing their safe release. “We understand the concern this incident has generated, particularly among residents and members of the university community around the Alabata axis. However, we appeal to everyone to remain calm and allow the relevant authorities to carry out their investigations and response. “It is equally important that information shared publicly is accurate and responsible. Unverified reports and speculation should be avoided, especially where they could interfere with ongoing security efforts. “The Union is deeply concerned about the safety of Hannah and the other victims. item.title: Violent campaigns
item.description: Barely two months to the 2027 general elections, there are rising cases of political violence across Nigeria, despite efforts by various bodies to discourage mayhem before, during and after the polls. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled to hold on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Assembly elections have been slated for February 6, 2026. In the last seven days, there have been cases of political violence in no less than seven states, with the latest in Lagos, where several supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) were injured after suspected political thugs disrupted a town hall meeting organised on Thursday by the party for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. There was also an incident in Zamfara State during an All Progressives Congress (APC) primary. INEC will obey court verdict on Atiku’s eligibility – Amupitan How 4 UNN students died after graduation party Other states that recorded violence within the period included Edo, Delta, Gombe and Cross River states. The incidents have been more frequent this year, with states like Katsina, Kebbi, Enugu, Ekiti, Ondo, Ebonyi, Osun and Nasarawa states all experiencing various forms of political violence. Prominent political actors have also threatened voters in ways that raised concerns over free, fair and credible polls in 2027. The National Peace Committee revealed recently that reports spanning August 19 to October 27 documented 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory. It also observed that political violence and thuggery led the violations with 33 incidents, closely followed by 29 cases of misinformation and disinformation and identified Kaduna, Edo, and Enugu as serious flashpoints for electoral violence. The European Union (EU) also expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of Nigeria’s general elections. EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, noted that these threats undermined democratic progress and discouraged citizens from participating freely in the electoral process. item.title: INEC Fixes Nov 28 For Nationwide Mock Accreditation Ahead Of 2027 General Elections
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has fixed November 28, 2026, for a nationwide mock accreditation exercise to test the effectiveness of its accreditation and electronic result transmission systems ahead of the 2027 general elections. ﻿ INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, announced this on Thursday in London during a high-level dialogue at Chatham House, organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI), under the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” Amupitan (right) spoke at Chatham House on Thursday, November 12, 2026. (Photo: X/@inecnigeria) Amupitan said that the exercise would simulate the presidential election and test the commission’s accreditation and electronic result transmission systems across all states of the federation. “On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said. The INEC chairman, who is a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, further stated that the exercise was part of measures to address technical challenges experienced during the 2023 general elections and strengthen the credibility of the 2027 polls. He disclosed that the commission had procured extra devices and reduced the maximum number of voters assigned to each BVAS machine from 1,250 to 850. According to him, polling units with more than 850 registered voters will be provided with multiple devices. Amupitan also said INEC was constructing climate-controlled storage facilities in all states to address the malfunction of BVAS devices previously linked to extreme heat and storage conditions during the 2023 elections. On electronic result transmission, he explained that the commission had introduced technical safeguards to prevent inaccurate results and figures reflecting over-voting from being uploaded to its Result Viewing Portal (IReV). He identified insecurity, logistics and result management as the commission’s three major priorities ahead of the 2027 elections. The INEC chairman said a post-2023 audit showed that the most significant failures in result management occurred at collation centres rather than polling units. He added that the commission had opted to upgrade its existing electoral technology rather than introduce an entirely new system because of the limited time before the 2027 elections. Amupitan also confirmed that INEC had received a substantial portion of its 2027 election budget but was awaiting the outstanding balance, part of which would fund the recruitment and welfare of ad hoc personnel. He said the commission had received assurances that the outstanding funds would be released before the end of November. item.title: US Congress Steps Up Scrutiny Of Trump, Nvidia After Huang Exit
item.description: Key US lawmakers on Thursday called for clarity on what the Trump administration knew about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chip giant announced his departure. Huang, now Nvidia’s former CEO, had pushed for looser rules on sales of US chips to China — crucial in the AI race — and the controversy has reenergized advocates of a hard line on Beijing, days before Donald Trump travels to China. “Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put US national security at risk,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said on social media. “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset,” he added. Huang, a co-founder of the AI chip giant, on Sunday acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence suspects her of working for Beijing, which has strongly denied the allegations. ‘Obvious Threat’ According to The New York Times, Trump was informed of the suspicions last year, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May. Trump said on Monday he knew “the FBI is looking into” the affair, adding that he expected Huang to be “in good shape.” He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy. U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP Huang was ultimately brought down by the scandal on Thursday, when the company’s board announced his departure, effective immediately. Lawmakers are also raising questions about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to impose restrictions on exports of the chips to China. Three Republican House committee chairmen had already said they wanted to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18. Democrats, who will take control of both chambers of Congress in January after winning the midterm elections, have also said they intend to look more closely into the affair. The top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees told Lutnick in a letter on Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s “scheme to approve and tax” Nvidia chip exports to Chinese firms linked to Beijing’s government and military. They accuse Lutnick and Trump of ignoring the “obvious national security threat” posed by the ties between Huang and a suspected Chinese intelligence agent, even though they had reportedly been informed of them. item.title: ‘His Support Base Still Strong’, Doherty Says Obi Can Repeat 2023 Feat In Lagos
item.description: The Lagos governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, says the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, retains a strong support base and has the backing to repeat his 2023 electoral performance in Lagos State. Doherty said this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, following an attack on the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos. He dismissed suggestions that Obi’s reception among Nigerians could be weakened by his defection from the Labour Party to the NDC, arguing that his appeal is rooted in his political philosophy rather than the platform on which he contests elections. “The idea of a new party is not something that we should hang our hat on anymore in our clime. Parties may be new, but the individuals involved are not new. “But the reception of Peter Obi today, that is how it is everywhere he goes. This is a man who is loved by the people. They view him as a different kind of politician, for good reason, and those of us who align with that philosophy and thinking,” he said. Doherty warned against underestimating Obi’s political influence, saying such an assumption could prove costly. “Anybody who is making a contrary case, time will tell. But I would advise them that if they are saying that just to downplay his significance, I think it will be a grave mistake on their part because his support base is still strong. I have seen it, not just today, we have seen it multiple times,” he added. He said the resistance by NDC supporters to the disruption of the party’s town hall meeting was evidence that the enthusiasm which characterised Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign had not diminished. “Those guys came in today probably thinking they would have an easy ride of it. They would come in and do what they might normally do, scatter things and people would run away. But people were not in that frame of mind. “We have laboured for this, and you cannot deprive us of it. And I think that spirit is alive and strong. To those who might think that, following 2023, people have lost some of that energy, I think, if anything, today should let us know that it is game on.” Attack On NDC supporters An injured NDC supporter during the attack by suspected thugs in Lagos Doherty also condemned the attack on the party’s town hall meeting at Classic Event Place in Oregun, Ikeja, describing it as “unprovoked” and “unnecessary.” Suspected political thugs invaded the venue on Thursday ahead of the arrival of Obi and his supporters. The attackers, said to be armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones, allegedly vandalised property and damaged several vehicles parked within the premises. However, NDC supporters resisted the attackers, confronting them and throwing chairs in an attempt to drive them away. The confrontation disrupted activities at the venue before security operatives intervened.
